messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
HOSPITAL COURSE:

The patient, a 28-day-old female newborn with right congenital aural atresia, was admitted to our emergency department with postauricular erythema and edema, accompanied by irritability, anorexia, and insomnia, without fever, since two days. On initial examination, the newborn had a small, deformed auricular tag on the right side with no external auditory meatus. Her weight was 3780 grams.
DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
TREATMENT:

The newborn was started immediately on meropenem and vancomycin i.v. Two days later, a mastoidectomy was performed, and abnormal bone was drilled or curetted away. Mastoid cells filled with granulation tissue were exenterated, and about 2 mL of pus were collected for culture. The antibiotic scheme continued for a total of four weeks.

CONDITION AT DISCHARGE:

The patient's postoperative course was unremarkable, with progressive resolution of signs of inflammation on mastoid area. The baby girl remained afebrile and her inflammation markers improved gradually. She left the hospital in a very good condition upon completion of her treatment. The baby has no problem two months after her operation, and her weight is 5.100 grams.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:

The patient should be observed for any signs of recurrence of symptoms and should follow up with her primary care provider regularly.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for admission is acute mastoiditis. Postauricular erythema and edema, mastoid cells filled with granulation tissue and pus, and treatment with IV antibiotics plus mastoidectomy all point to this, in a newborn with congenital aural atresia. Acute mastoiditis belongs to chapter H (diseases of the ear and mastoid process), category H70 (mastoiditis and related conditions). The congenital atresia (Q16) is a background condition, not the reason for admission.

CODE: H70
